metadata.note: The Southern Indiana Railway's own passenger years (it took over the Evansville and Richmond on 4 Jun 1897 and ran the line until its receiver handed over to the Chicago, Terre Haute and Southeastern on 31 Dec 1910), plus two predecessors that ran public trains under their own names. Six features, each drawn only for its report's drawable span: Evansville and Terre Haute (operating the Evansville and Richmond) Elnora - Westport 1893 [ANCHOR]; Bedford Belt Bedford - Oolitic 1893-1896; Southern Indiana Elnora - Bedford 1898-1900 [OPEN], Bedford - Westport 1898-1900 [OPEN], Elnora - Linton 1900 [ANCHOR], Terre Haute - Linton 1900-1903 [OPEN]. All geometry is reused from the successor layer chicago_terre_haute_and_southeastern_railway.geojson, which draws the same track, cut at Elnora, Linton and Oolitic.
metadata.ownership_split: Evansville and Richmond Railroad, operated by the Evansville and Terre Haute 'as a separate unit' to 27 Feb 1894 (feature drawn in E&TH colour, pulled programmatically from evansville_hub.geojson feature evv-eth-evansville-terre-haute, company string 'Evansville and Terre Haute Railroad') -> E&R receiver 27 Feb 1894 - 4 Jun 1897 (not drawn: no passenger year) -> Southern Indiana Railway from 4 Jun 1897 (first passenger evidence 10 Jan 1898): a Rule 4 split, new colour. Bedford Belt Railway (own company, new colour) -> leased to the Southern Indiana 1 Jul 1898 (a lease, so a split; the lease years are not drawn). NOT a split: the Southern Indiana receivership of 19 Aug 1908 - 31 Dec 1910 (the receiver ran the SI's own trains). 1 Jan 1911 -> CTH&SE, already drawn in its own layer.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn, per the report's drawable fields: [E3] Evansville and Richmond under its receiver, 27 Feb 1894 - 4 Jun 1897 (no dated passenger evidence; the March 1897 washout closed Bedford - Westport); [5] Terre Haute - Clinton - West Dana, opened 1905 (no Southern Indiana-era passenger year; CTH&SE passenger service is dated only c.1916); [6] Blackhawk - Hymera - Sullivan (Fowler lists it as a passenger line but dates no stop; no passenger evidence in any era; not the THI&E Sullivan interurban); [7] Bedford Belt under the Southern Indiana lease 1898 - 1910 (public service dated 1893, 1896 and 1915 but nothing in the lease years); [8] Latta - Hawton coal branch (only a 1937 Milwaukee miners' train is dated); [9] Chicago Southern, Chicago Heights/Faithorn - Quaker, Ill., SI-operated Nov 1907 - Aug 1908 (Rule 1: freight only throughout - ICC, Fowler and Blackhawk RHS agree). [C1]/[C2] CTH&SE and Milwaukee eras are drawn in chicago_terre_haute_and_southeastern_railway.geojson. Also not drawn: the Seymour Junction - Seymour station stub, the Dark Hollow spur, and the Bedford Belt beyond Oolitic.
metadata.freight_only_check: Every feature ends at its last confirmed passenger year; none has a freight-only tail. The only freight-only line in the report, the Chicago Southern [9] (including the SI's 1907-08 operation of it), is excluded. Terre Haute - West Dana, Terre Haute - Sullivan, the Bedford Belt in the lease years and Latta - Hawton are omitted as unconfirmed, not as freight-only findings.
metadata.horsecar_check: None: steam railroad throughout; nothing trimmed.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: 1. THE 1904-1910 GAP, the biggest: no confirmed Southern Indiana passenger year after 1903 anywhere, and none after 1900 east of Linton. Service almost certainly ran continuously to 31 Dec 1910 (the CTH&SE inherited a working passenger network, dated c.1916), but no 1904-1910 timetable, Official Guide listing or news item was found. [OPEN] ends: si-elnora-bedford 1900, si-bedford-westport 1900, si-terre-haute-linton 1903. Best next sources: an Official Guide of 1905-1910, Poor's Manual 1905-1910, Indiana Railroad Commission reports (from 1905), the Terre Haute Tribune / Bedford Daily Mail. 2. [ANCHOR] eth-er-elnora-westport 1893 only: section opening dates of the E&R (built 1886 - c.1890) not found; the 1894-97 receiver years have no evidence; whether the Guide printed the service under the E&R's or the E&TH's name not checked. 3. [ANCHOR] si-elnora-linton 1900 only; passenger trains at the 22 Jan 1900 opening not directly confirmed. 4. Elnora - Bedford June 1897 - Jan 1898: whether SI trains ran west of the washout is unknown; drawn from 1898. 5. Bedford Belt: who worked the trains in 1893-98; nothing dated 1897-1914. 6. Terre Haute - West Dana (1905) and Blackhawk - Sullivan: no Southern Indiana-era passenger date. 7. The Southern Indiana's Terre Haute passenger terminal in 1900-03 (Vandalia depot or its own) not established. 8. All headways and speeds are estimates (the only count is IJ-1900's three trains each way at Terre Haute).
metadata.conflicts: IJ-1900 gives Terre Haute - Westport as 113 miles; Fowler's mileposts give about 150 (121.8 + 27.9) - recorded, Fowler's mileage used for the length checks. Bedford Belt: drawn 1893-1896 as the span between two Official Guide listings (Fowler's 1893 z letter and 1896G header); if joining two listings is not accepted the fallback is two anchors, 1893 and 1896.
metadata.cross_report: Successor eras: research/branches/chicago_terre_haute_and_southeastern_railway.txt and layer chicago_terre_haute_and_southeastern_railway.geojson (CTH&SE 1911-1921, Milwaukee Road from 1921). The narrow-gauge Bedford and Bloomfield (Bedford - Switz City) was never part of the Southern Indiana; it is drawn in monon_railroad.geojson.

properties.geometry_quality: Reused geometry, no straight-line legs: 100.7 mi Elnora - Westport against ~102 mi (ICC) / 103.6 mi (Fowler) documented. Elnora - Bedford (38.1 mi) is the CTH&SE layer's Terre Haute - Bedford feature cut at Elnora (vertex 80, 0.26 mi from the Nominatim village point; Fowler milepost 46.1 vs 45.4 traced from Terre Haute); Elnora - Crane is active Indiana Rail Road track, Crane - Bedford abandoned grade. BEDFORD CONNECTOR: the CTH&SE layer's Terre Haute - Bedford and Bedford - Westport features do not meet (0.94 mi apart, both at Bedford); this feature bridges them with 1.0 mi of OpenHistoricalMap railway way 198556259 (rail, start_date 1900, end_date 1990, no operator tag; the same way continues to Westport, so identified as this line by position), not a straight line. Where Bedford station stood on it was not pinned. Bedford - Westport is the CTH&SE Bedford - Westport feature unchanged (one OSM abandoned way tagged old_railway_operator=Milwaukee; it passes Seymour on the north at Seymour Junction and does NOT draw the 0.8 mi Seymour Junction - Seymour station stub, which Fowler's mileage counts twice - the main reason the trace is short). Elnora end: in 1893 Elnora was the E&R's west terminus (junction with the Evansville and Indianapolis); the Elnora - Linton line west of it did not exist until 22 Jan 1900 and is not drawn here. LATER ALIGNMENT: the geometry is the line as OSM/OHM record it at its last (Milwaukee-era / abandonment) state; no realignment after the drawn year is backed out, and none is known to the research. The 1941 Naval Ammunition Depot at Crane (Burns City) may have altered the line there; not checked.

segments.note: Evansville and Richmond Railroad passenger service Elnora - Bedford - Seymour - Westport, operated by the Evansville and Terre Haute 'as a separate unit' (ICC valuation) until the E&R's receivership of 27 Feb 1894. Fowler's z letter (the 1893 Official Guide) is on six stops on both sides of Bedford and on the Seymour - Westport leg: Burns [Burns City/Crane], Huffs [Blankenship], Bossert [Mount Olive], Millersburg [Shawswick], Courtland [Cortland], Springer [Grammer]. The line was built 1886 - c.1890; no section opening dates were found. [ANCHOR] This is a single proven year: service certainly ran wider in both directions (the line was open c.1890 - March 1897, when a washout closed Bedford - Westport), but no other year is confirmed. Do not widen without evidence. Colour and company are the E&TH's because it ran the trains (Rule 4); whether the 1893 Guide printed the service under the E&R's or the E&TH's name was not checked. The E&R receiver's years 27 Feb 1894 - 4 Jun 1897 have no passenger evidence and are not drawn; the Southern Indiana reopened the line in Jan 1898 (see the Southern Indiana features). Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE; no timetable was seen.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler, branchline.uk Indiana Railroads lines 112 and 117, z (1893 Official Guide) letters at Burns, Huffs, Bossert, Millersburg, Courtland and Springer - the only source for the 1893 anchor. Operator (E&TH 'as a separate unit' to 27 Feb 1894) from the ICC valuation's E&R corporate history. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Bedford Belt Railway passenger service Bedford - North Bedford (6th Street) - Dark Hollow Junction - Oolitic, the limestone-quarry belt line, opened 1 May 1893 (ICC valuation). Two Official Guide listings bound the span: Fowler's 'Lime Stone z(tm)' marks Oolitic as the passenger terminus in the 1893 Guide, and Fowler heads the line 'ex Bedford Belt; 1896G', a stop list from the 1896 Guide. Drawn 1893-1896 as the span between those two listings; each end is a listing, not a known start or end. Who physically worked the trains (the E&R/E&TH or the Monon) was not established; the company is the Bedford Belt, which owned the line until the Southern Indiana lease of 1 Jul 1898. Nothing dated 1897 - 1910 was found (the Southern Indiana lease years are not drawn; see the layer's omitted field). Headway 1440 min (one round trip a day) is an ESTIMATE.
sources: Segment-level: Fowler, branchline.uk Indiana Railroads line 116 ('Lime Stone z' = 1893 Official Guide; line header '1896G' = 1896 Official Guide); opening date and ownership from the ICC valuation's Bedford Belt corporate history. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Southern Indiana Railway (formerly the Evansville and Richmond, taken over 4 Jun 1897) passenger trains Elnora - Odon - Burns City - Blankenship - Tunnel Switch - Indian Springs - Williams - Coxton - Bedford. Start: the Indianapolis Journal of 10 Jan 1898 announces the road 'reopened for freight and passenger traffic to-day', with a station list beginning at Elnora. Whether trains ran Elnora - Bedford between June 1897 and Jan 1898 (only the line east of Bedford was washed out) is not established, so 1897 is not drawn. 1900: Fowler's 'Tunnel Switch 1900G' (1900 Official Guide) and the Indianapolis Journal of 18 Sep 1900 (Terre Haute opening, Westport - Terre Haute excursions over this leg). [OPEN] The end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: the Southern Indiana ran the line until its receiver handed over to the Chicago, Terre Haute and Southeastern on 31 Dec 1910, and the CTH&SE ran passenger trains Terre Haute - Westport c.1916 (ICC valuation), so service almost certainly continued, but no source in hand dates a later Southern Indiana passenger year. Do not extend without evidence. The 19 Aug 1908 receivership is not an ownership change for the map. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE (IJ-1900 reports three regular trains each way at Terre Haute; whether all three ran through to Bedford is not stated).
sources: Segment-level: Indianapolis Journal 10 Jan 1898 p.6 ('reopened for freight and passenger traffic', station list) for 1898; Fowler line 112 'Tunnel Switch 1900G' and Indianapolis Journal 18 Sep 1900 p.6 for 1900; ICC valuation for the takeover and 31 Dec 1910 handover. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Southern Indiana Railway passenger trains Bedford - Shawswick (Millersburg) - Heltonville - Norman - Freetown - Cortland - Seymour - Azalia - Elizabethtown - Sardinia - Westport. The line had been closed by a washout in March 1897 under the Evansville and Richmond receiver; the Indianapolis Journal of 10 Jan 1898 announces it reopened 'for freight and passenger traffic to-day', 'all restrictions covering the road east of Bedford are removed', with the full station list to Westport. Fowler: 'Westport [Big Four Depot 1898G]' (1898 Official Guide). 1900: the Indianapolis Journal of 18 Sep 1900 says the road 'will run excursions to Terre Haute from the other end of the line - Westport'. [OPEN] The end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: the Southern Indiana ran the line until its receiver handed over to the Chicago, Terre Haute and Southeastern on 31 Dec 1910, and the CTH&SE ran passenger trains Terre Haute - Westport c.1916 (ICC valuation), so service almost certainly continued, but no source in hand dates a later Southern Indiana passenger year. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 720 min is an ESTIMATE; no Southern Indiana timetable was seen.
sources: Segment-level: Indianapolis Journal 10 Jan 1898 p.6 (reopening east of Bedford, station list to Westport) and Fowler lines 112/117 'Westport [Big Four Depot 1898G]' for 1898; Indianapolis Journal 18 Sep 1900 p.6 (Westport - Terre Haute excursions) for 1900; ICC valuation for the 1897 washout and the 31 Dec 1910 handover. Headway not sourced (estimate).

segments.note: Southern Indiana Railway passenger trains Terre Haute - Hulman Street - Keller (Ferrel) - Blackhawk - Lewis - Coalmont - Jasonville - Latta - Vicksburg - Linton. Opened 17 Sep 1900 (ICC valuation); the Indianapolis Journal of 18 Sep 1900: 'The Southern Indiana road began doing business in Terre Haute yesterday, running three regular passenger trains each way'. 1903: Fowler 'Keller [Ferrel 1903Glist]', Ferrel in the 1903 Official Guide station list. Also, weakly, the Richmond Daily Palladium of 9 Mar 1901 (a Linton woman given a lifetime pass for saving trains from a wreck) - not used for the span. [OPEN] The end year is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end: the Southern Indiana ran the line until its receiver handed over to the Chicago, Terre Haute and Southeastern on 31 Dec 1910, and the CTH&SE ran passenger trains Terre Haute - Westport c.1916 (ICC valuation), so service almost certainly continued, but no source in hand dates a later Southern Indiana passenger year. Do not extend without evidence. Headway 480 min is derived from the three trains each way reported at the 1900 opening, spread over a day; it is an ESTIMATE for the later years. SOURCE ODDITY recorded: IJ-1900 calls Terre Haute - Westport 113 miles, against about 150 by Fowler's mileposts.
sources: Segment-level: Indianapolis Journal 18 Sep 1900 p.6 (opening day, three passenger trains each way) and ICC valuation (opened 17 Sep 1900) for 1900; Fowler line 112 'Ferrel 1903Glist' (1903 Official Guide) for 1903; Richmond Daily Palladium 9 Mar 1901 p.2 as weak corroboration only. Headway derived from IJ-1900's train count (estimate).
